**Claim 229513 (carrier claim): the model scores it below average for denial risk.**

The model gives a denial probability of 0.0869. The validation-set average is 0.1805, so this claim is 0.48 times the average, or -9.4 percentage points versus the average. The denial label in this project is synthetic. It was built from risk rules, so this is not a real payer decision.

The SHAP explanation starts from a baseline probability of 0.1404. All six top features lower the risk:

- **LINE_PLACE_OF_SRVC_CD (value 11):** -13% on the odds. The project data dictionary has no entry for this field.
- **HCPCS_CD (null):** -9% on the odds. The dictionary describes it as the procedure or service code billed. No code was recorded on this claim.
- **CARR_LINE_PRCNG_LCLTY_CD (23):** -8% on the odds. It is undocumented in the dictionary.
- **CARR_CLM_BLG_NPI_NUM:** -7% on the odds. It is undocumented in the dictionary.
- **PRNCPAL_DGNS_CD (Z733):** -7% on the odds. The dictionary describes it as the principal diagnosis (ICD-10-CM).
- **TAX_NUM:** -6% on the odds. It is undocumented in the dictionary.

The 153 features not shown add a combined -0.005 log-odds.

The model weighs these features. That doesn't mean they cause or prevent a denial. Four of the six top features have no dictionary entry, so I can't say what they represent. I didn't search the policy documents, so I can't say whether any policy applies to this claim.
